title: paged KV cache: block allocator reuse and pinning optimizations
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: The paged KV cache block manager was suffering from allocator churn and occasional tail-latency spikes under high-concurrency continuous-batching workloads. This PR introduces a reuse-friendly block allocator, improved pinning semantics to avoid premature eviction of in-flight KV pages, and several micro-optimizations to reduce per-request locking and copy overhead.

What changed (single consolidated description): Implement a slab-style block allocator with reuse buckets keyed by block size; add a pinCount-based pinning API that avoids moving blocks while they are referenced by active requests; replace a global mutex in BlockManager with a combination of fine-grained shard locks and an atomic freelist for hot-path allocations; add heuristics to prefer eviction of cold blocks and to coalesce adjacent free blocks during free-time instead of during allocation; expose new metrics (kv.block_reuse_hits, kv.block_pin_conflicts, kv.block_frag_ratio).

Benchmarks: microbenchmarks (local perf harness) show ~9-12% tail-latency p95 improvement for 512-token median requests with continuous batching enabled, and ~15-20% throughput improvement for small-request workloads due to reduced allocation overhead. Integration tests with the perf-canary harness showed sustained throughput increase of ~18% under simulated 4k QPS multi-tenant traces.

Compatibility and rollout: Behavior is backwards compatible at the API level. The new pinning semantics are opt-in via a feature flag `kv_pinning_v2` in runtime config; rollout plan is staged: enable for internal perf-canary first, then enable for a subset of Hosted API tenants, then flip global. There are migration guards to fall back to the legacy allocator if unexpected errors occur.

Testing: Unit tests for allocator reuse logic and pin/unpin races were added; integration tests cover eviction edge cases and high-concurrency allocation; extended stress tests in perf-canary for 48 hours without regression.

Migration checklist: [x] add new allocator implementation; [x] add pinning API; [x] add metrics and tracing; [x] add unit/integration tests; [x] feature-flag gate and rollout plan; [x] documentation update for runtime config.

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps memory accounting unchanged; follow-up work will introduce adaptive bucket sizing and further fragmentation reduction based on observed kv.block_frag_ratio.
